You are a dependency vulnerability triage agent. You receive the parsed contents of one dependency file: the dependencies whose exact versions are known, and the entries that could not be checked.

Tools:
- check_packages: known vulnerabilities per exact package version (OSV), with CISA KEV status and EPSS.
- get_vulnerability: NVD details for one vulnerability. Slow (rate limited); use it only when you need details.

Process:
1. Call check_packages once with every entry under "dependencies", using ecosystem, name and version exactly as given.
2. If you need details for a few vulnerabilities, call get_vulnerability for those only.
3. Return the final report as JSON that follows the response schema.

Report rules:
- Grounding: list only vulnerabilities returned by check_packages, and use the tool's `id` field as the id. Never add vulnerabilities from memory. Suspicions the tools cannot confirm (for example vulnerable transitive dependencies) go in `notes`, never in `packages`.
- Completeness: include every vulnerability the tool returned for every vulnerable package, including low-priority ones.
- Ranking: rank 1 is the most urgent; ranks are unique across the whole report. Every CISA KEV-listed vulnerability ranks above every vulnerability that is not KEV-listed. Within each group, higher EPSS ranks higher; use severity to break ties.
- kev: true only if the tool's `kev` field for that vulnerability is an object (listed), otherwise false.
- upgrade_to (per package): the lowest version that fixes ALL of that package's vulnerabilities, not only the most urgent one. Choose it from the fixed versions the tool returned for that package. Fixed versions often belong to different release lines (for example 2.3.1 / 2.12.2 / 2.15.0 for three branches); the version you choose must not be affected by any of the package's vulnerabilities and must not be lower than the installed version. Use null when no single version fixes all of them, and say why in `reason`.
- A vulnerability with `last_affected` affects versions up to and including that version; versions above it are not affected by it, so it does not stop you from choosing a higher fixed version.
- The same vulnerability id can affect two packages; list it under each affected package.
- unchecked: repeat every entry of the input "unchecked" list with its reason, plus anything else you could not check.
- Do not list packages that have no vulnerabilities.
- Write `summary`, `reason` and `notes` in Korean.

{"summary":"13개 Maven 직접 의존성 중 7개 패키지에서 취약점 7건(CVE 기준 고유 6건, spring-context 취약점 3건 포함)이 확인되었습니다. CISA KEV에 등록된 항목은 없습니다. 가장 시급한 것은 spring-context의 CVE-2022-22968과 hsqldb의 CVE-2022-41853(CRITICAL)입니다. spring-context 3.2.6은 지원 종료 라인이므로 6.1.20 이상으로의 업그레이드가 필요하며, 메이저 버전 차이로 인한 호환성 검토가 필요합니다.","packages":[{"package":"Maven/org.springframework:spring-context@3.2.6.RELEASE","upgrade_to":"6.1.20","reason":"확인된 3개 취약점을 모두 해결하는 가장 낮은 버전은 6.1.20입니다. CVE-2025-22233은 6.1.20 미만의 6.1.x 버전이 영향을 받으므로 6.1.14는 불충분하고, 5.3.x(5.3.19 등)는 CVE-2024-38820과 CVE-2025-22233의 영향 범위(last_affected 5.3.40, 5.3.39)에 포함됩니다. 3.x에서 6.x로의 메이저 업그레이드이므로 API 호환성 검토가 필요합니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2022-22968","rank":3,"priority":"high","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2024-38820","rank":6,"priority":"medium","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2025-22233","rank":7,"priority":"low","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/org.hsqldb:hsqldb@2.3.2","upgrade_to":"2.7.1","reason":"확인된 취약점(CVE-2022-41853, CRITICAL, 원격 코드 실행)을 해결하는 버전은 2.7.1입니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2022-41853","rank":2,"priority":"critical","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/org.hibernate:hibernate-core@4.3.7.Final","upgrade_to":"5.3.20.Final","reason":"CVE-2019-14900은 5.3.18에서, CVE-2020-25638은 5.3.20.Final에서 수정되므로 두 취약점을 모두 해결하는 가장 낮은 버전은 5.3.20.Final입니다. 4.x에서 5.x로의 메이저 업그레이드이므로 호환성 검토가 필요합니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2020-25638","rank":4,"priority":"high","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2019-14900","rank":5,"priority":"medium","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/junit:junit@4.12","upgrade_to":"4.13.1","reason":"CVE-2020-15250은 4.13.1에서 수정됩니다. test 스코프 의존성이므로 운영 배포에는 직접 영향이 적습니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2020-15250","rank":8,"priority":"medium","kev":false}]}],"unchecked":[],"notes":["KEV 등재 취약점은 없으며, 순위는 EPSS 점수 기준(동점 시 심각도)으로 매겼습니다.","spring-orm, spring-aspects, spring-test는 OSV에서 취약점이 조회되지 않았지만, spring-context와 동일한 Spring 버전 라인이므로 spring-context를 6.1.20 이상으로 올릴 때 함께 맞추는 것을 권장합니다.","hibernate-entitymanager 4.3.7.Final도 취약점이 조회되지 않았으나, hibernate-core를 5.3.20.Final로 올릴 때 버전을 함께 맞추어야 합니다.","직접 의존성만 확인했습니다. 전이 의존성(transitive dependencies)은 resolved dependency tree가 필요하므로 점검하지 않았습니다.","부모 POM(io.github.snyk:todolist-mvc:0.0.1-SNAPSHOT)의 속성과 관리 버전이 적용된 상태로 점검했습니다.","cglib, aspectjweaver, c3p0, commons-collections, hibernate-jpa-2.0-api는 OSV에서 알려진 취약점이 없었으나, 이는 안전을 보장하지 않습니다(알 수 없는 패키지명도 같은 결과가 나옵니다)."]}
thinking:
There are no KEV entries, so I'm ranking the non-KEV group by EPSS, using severity to break ties. Spring-context 3.2.6.RELEASE has two CVEs to weigh: CVE-2022-22968 with EPSS 0.05666 and HIGH severity, and CVE-2024-38820 with EPSS 0.00617 and a last_affected of 5.3.

I'm checking the fixed versions for spring-context 3.2.6. The tool lists 5.2.21, 5.3.19, 6.1.14, 6.1.20 and 6.2.7, and CVE-2025-22233 (EPSS 0.00442) also applies. I'm weighing whether 5.2.21 clears all three CVEs, since the 5.3 last_affected cutoffs don't obviously cover the 5.2 line.

I'm weighing 5.2.21 against the 5.3 cutoffs: CVE-2025-22233 stops at 5.3.39 and CVE-2024-38820 at 5.3.40, so 5.2.21 looks clear of both, though I still need to pick the lowest fixed version the tool returned that avoids every CVE.

Checking whether 6.1.20 is the lowest version that clears all three CVEs, since 5.2.21 is the only lower candidate and the tool didn't list it as a fix for CVE-2024-38820.

I'm checking whether 6.1.20 is safe on the 6.x line, since the tool's fixed versions for CVE-2022-22968 are only 5.2.21 and 5.3.19, and it gives nothing about 6.x for that CVE.

I'm working out whether 6.1.20 is the right pick, since it's the lowest tool-listed version that fixes CVE-2025-22233 as well as CVE-2024-38820. Moving from 3.2 to the 6.x line is a big jump, but the fixed-version rule is what decides it. 6.1.14 can't be the answer, because the tool lists 6.1.20 as the fix for CVE-2025-22233 and 6.1.14 would still be affected by it.

I'm ranking the findings by EPSS, and now I'm working out the spring-context upgrade target: 6.1.20 is the lowest fixed version that covers all three CVEs. Moving across to 6.x is a major-version change, so the reason should flag that it needs a compatibility review, and I should note that the other Spring modules should be aligned to the same version.

I'm ranking the findings by EPSS and assigning severity labels, with the spring-context CVE-2022-22968 at high and hsqldb's CVE-2022-41853 at critical.

I'm settling the hibernate-core upgrade: 5.3.20.Final is the lowest version that clears both CVEs, since 5.3.18 misses the fix for CVE-2020-25638.

Hibernate-core's 5.3.20.Final is the lowest tool-listed version that clears both CVEs, so I'm settling on that. I'm also noting hibernate-entitymanager has no known vulns but should move in step. hsqldb goes to 2.7.1, and junit to 4.13.1 since it's test scope only. For spring-context I'm weighing 6.1.20 again, with the rank question still open.

I'm weighing whether 5.2.21 might be the lowest safe pick after all: the tool lists it as a fix for CVE-2022-22968, and the OSV ranges for the 5.3-line CVEs don't seem to reach back into 5.2, though the tool doesn't list it as a fix for them. That ambiguity is what I still need to settle.

I'm still torn on whether 5.2.21 could be the lowest safe pick: it's a tool-returned fix for CVE-2022-22968, and the affected ranges for the 5.3-line CVEs seem to start at 5.3.0, but the tool never lists it as a fix for 38820 or 22233. Since I can't confirm it from the data, I'm leaning toward 6.1.20 as the version that's clearly covered.

I'm settling on 6.1.20 as the spring-context target, since 5.2.21 only shows up as a fix for CVE-2022-22968 and the tool doesn't list it for the other two, and 5.2 is an end-of-life line. The reason should note the move from 3.x to 6.x is a major jump that needs a compatibility check, and the other Spring modules should be upgraded to match.

Now I'm settling the output format: a single-line JSON with Korean strings and no newlines, and I need to be careful with the quotes inside the values.
